beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Access is a switch somebody flips, and it completes in a minute. Absorption happens in other people's weeks, at their pace, for their reasons.
beats.got: Access and uptake get reported as one number. They are different things, and uptake moves at human speed.

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had.
beats.got: Leaders didn't act on analysis done by people they trusted, because it wasn't theirs. I know that from both my change negotiations.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: You can copy an agent's setup, but the person who answers for it stays behind. So a shared agent is never really shared.

beats.trigger: Pick the one your teammate's week can take in.
beats.got: Each way of sharing asks something different of the receiver. Match it to their week.

beats.trigger: Somebody they trust has to have used it first and said so.
beats.got: The agent competes with the spreadsheet or the colleague people use today, and trust travels through a person.

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: Talk to one person about how they do the job today before building more.

beats.trigger: Who gets your context, who gets a skill, who wants only the output, and who would use an @mention?
beats.got: Different colleagues need different ways of sharing. I'd sort my HR partners that way.

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks.

take_homes: Access is not uptake. Giving everyone the tool says little about whether anyone uses it. That is the honest answer for the leadership team, and it is better than yes or no on headcount.

Before I roll anything out to a team, I interview one colleague about how they do the job today and ask what would have to be true for them to switch. Every plan gets a technical half and a people half, with named owners.
You don't share the agent, you share a piece of it. The person who answers for it doesn't come along in the folder.

monday.move: Ask one HR business partner how they build the weekly people-metrics summary today, and what would make them drop that way. Only after that, sketch an agent for it.
monday.who: One HR business partner from my team
monday.stop_condition: If they say they trust the current way and see no problem to fix, I don't build anything.
monday.blocker: The data is employee data. I have to ask the works council and the DPO first, and I haven't yet.

misconception.why: The module never said roles stay or go. But it showed that rollout happens at human pace and needs someone who answers for it. That makes 'which roles go first' look too simple. I still think headcount will come up, and the module has no answer to it.

one_line: The tool parts were over my head, but 'access is not absorption' and 'your people plan can't have unnamed roles' are things I'll repeat in the leadership meeting.
